questions.question: A 4-digit number greater than 5000 is randomly formed from the digits 0, 1, 3, 5, 7 (repetition allowed). What is the probability of forming a number divisible by 5?
solutionSteps: Total numbers > 5000: Thousands place can be 5 or 7.
Thousands 5 or 7 (2 ways). Hundreds (5), Tens (5), Units (2). Total $2\times5\times5\times2 = 100$.

questions.question: If 7 relatives (3 ladies and 4 gentlemen) are to be invited for dinner, find the probability that at least one lady is included in a selection of 3 guests.
solutionSteps: At least one lady = Total - No lady = $35 - 4 = 31$.

questions.question: Two dice are thrown simultaneously. The probability that the product of the numbers appearing is even is
solutionSteps: Product is odd only if both numbers are odd.
Odd numbers on a die: 1, 3, 5 (3 outcomes).

questions.question: If A and B are mutually exclusive events such that $P(A) = 0.35$ and $P(B) = 0.45$, then $P(A' \cap B')$ is
solutionSteps: Since mutually exclusive, $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.35 + 0.45 = 0.8$.

questions.question: A 5-digit number is formed using the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 without repetition. The probability that it is divisible by 4 is
solutionSteps: Total 5-digit numbers: First place 4 options (1-4), rest $4!$. Total $4 \times 24 = 96$.
Divisible by 4 if last two digits are: 04, 12, 20, 24, 32, 40.
No 0 at end (12, 24, 32): $3 \times (2 \times 2 \times 1) = 12$ (First digit can't be 0).

questions.question: Four cards are drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. What is the probability of obtaining 3 diamonds and one spade?
solutionSteps: Favorable: Select 3 Diamonds from 13 ($^{13}C_3$) and 1 Spade from 13 ($^{13}C_1$).

questions.question: The letters of the word 'SOCIETY' are placed at random in a row. What is the probability that the three vowels come together?
solutionSteps: Vowels: O, I, E. Consonants: S, C, T, Y.

questions.question: Three numbers are chosen from the set ${1, 2, \dots, 20}$. Find the probability that they are in A.P.
solutionSteps: For $a, b, c$ in AP, $a+c=2b$. $a$ and $c$ must have same parity.
